title: Co-op Spotify: A Discovery Engine for Roles
concept:
=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: adjacent-vertical (probability 0.12)
Title: Co-op Spotify: A Discovery Engine for Roles
Thesis: Borrow Spotify's discovery DNA — Discover Weekly, Daily Mixes, Wrapped — and apply it to NUworks SME roles delivered through Microsoft Teams.
Why this frame: Spotify already solved the brand-fixation problem in music: it pulls listeners out of Top-40 ruts via collaborative filtering, themed mixes, and editorial curation. Mapping that pattern onto co-op discovery is a one-to-one analogy that first-years intuitively understand on day one.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Jordan Liu
  Role: First-year Business Analytics undergraduate, D'Amore-McKim
  Context: Lives in International Village, opens Teams daily for class group chats, uses Spotify Discover Weekly every Monday morning, has already submitted three applications to Goldman, JPMorgan, and McKinsey before October of freshman year.
  Emotional state: Quietly anxious under a confident exterior — believes brand-name placements are the only credible outcome and feels embarrassed at the idea of working at a company his high-school friends won't recognize.
  Pain points:
    - Knows the names of five employers and assumes the other 3,800 on NUworks are 'backup' or 'lesser'
    - NUworks search returns 200+ analytics roles in flat list view — paralyzing, so he defaults to brand filters
    - Has no peer signal on which SMEs are actually great — no one's posted a TikTok about a 40-person Cambridge fintech
    - Reads job descriptions written in stiff corporate HR voice and cannot tell what the work actually feels like
  JTBD: When I have ten spare minutes between classes, I want to discover co-op opportunities that fit who I'm becoming, so I can build a balanced application list without spending Saturday nights doomscrolling NUworks.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Strategic Co-op Director (Liz's team): Curates weekly 'Editorial Playlists' of vetted SME roles and approves the AI's discovery criteria each Monday before digests ship.
  - Co-op Faculty Coordinator: Reviews aggregate engagement data in Power BI to identify cohort taste shifts and intervene with at-risk students whose taste profiles stay locked on brand names.
  - Data Systems Admin: Maintains the Power Automate flow from NUworks → SharePoint → Teams and tunes the daily batch export schedule.
  - SME Employer Partner: Submits a 60-word 'liner note' describing what the work actually feels like, which the AI weaves into the audio brief.

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Jordan receives his first 'Discover Co-op Weekly' card in Teams on a Monday at 8:03 AM — 10 SME roles bundled into themed mixes like 'Because you liked fintech,' 'Fresh finds in Boston analytics,' and 'Founders under 40.' He taps play on a 45-second audio brief about a Cambridge analytics SME during his walk to class, hearts it before reaching Snell Library, and the system silently logs the signal to refine next week's mix.

USE CASES (10) — the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Browse Discover Co-op Weekly
     Trigger: Monday 8 AM Teams notification: 'Your Discover Co-op Weekly is ready — 10 fresh roles, just for you.'
     Flow: Jordan opens Teams → sees the Co-op Discovery bot at top of activity feed → taps the digest card → adaptive card unfurls with album-art-style tiles for 10 roles grouped into 3 themed mixes → scrolls, taps a tile to expand → either hearts, skips, or opens the role detail.
     AI role: Collaborative filter scores 200+ NUworks SME roles against Jordan's declared major, hearted history, and the application patterns of anonymized peer cohorts, then a themed-mix composer clusters the top 10 into 3 narratively-labeled groups.
     Outcome: Jordan finishes the digest in 90 seconds with at least 2 hearts logged and 1 role saved to apply later — entirely inside Teams, no new portal.
  2. Listen to an Audio Role Brief
     Trigger: Jordan taps the speaker icon on a role tile while walking between Snell and IV.
     Flow: Inline audio player appears within the Teams adaptive card → 45-second narrated brief begins → progress bar animates → at end, three buttons appear: Heart, Skip, Save → Jordan taps Heart → animation confirms.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 rewrites the dry NUworks JD into conversational second-person script; a TTS layer (Azure Speech via Power Automate) generates the audio file, cached in SharePoint.
     Outcome: Jordan absorbs the texture of an SME role hands-free — discovers it feels exciting in ways the text JD never conveyed.
  3. Skip / Heart / Apply Signals
     Trigger: Any interaction with a role tile during the digest.
     Flow: Tap heart → tile pulses pink, signal logged → tap skip → tile dims, system asks 'too corporate? too small? wrong city?' with three quick-reply chips → tap apply → deep-link opens NUworks application page in browser.
     AI role: Embedding model updates Jordan's taste profile vector after each signal; skip-reason chips train the negative space of the recommender.
     Outcome: Every micro-interaction sharpens next Monday's digest — Jordan feels the system listening.
  4. Explore a Daily Mix by Theme
     Trigger: Jordan opens the Co-op Discovery tab in Teams mid-week and sees 4 Daily Mix tiles: Fintech Foundations, Boston Builders, Mission-Driven, Hidden Cambridge.
     Flow: Taps Boston Builders → sub-card unfurls with 8 roles from sub-50-employee Boston SMEs → can heart/skip individually or 'shuffle' to reorder.
     AI role: Themed Mix Composer (Gemini 3.1 Pro) writes the mix's narrative hook ('Local founders building the next generation of data tools') and selects roles whose embeddings cluster around the theme centroid.
     Outcome: Jordan realizes there are 8 roles in Cambridge alone he'd never heard of — aperture widens without anyone lecturing him.
  5. See 'Because You Hearted X' Recommendations
     Trigger: Jordan revisits a role detail he hearted last week.
     Flow: Below the role, a horizontal carousel appears labeled 'Because you hearted Klaviyo Analytics Co-op' → 5 lookalike roles → each tagged with the similarity signal (industry, team size, tech stack).
     AI role: Cosine similarity on role embeddings surfaces lookalikes; Claude generates the human-readable 'because' justification per tile.
     Outcome: Jordan moves from one hearted role to applying to four adjacent ones in a single sitting.
  6. Editorial Picks from Co-op Advisors
     Trigger: Friday afternoon Teams card: 'Liz's Picks This Week — hand-curated by the Co-op Strategy team.'
     Flow: Tap card → 5 roles with a short advisor note (avatar + 2-sentence rationale) for each → Jordan reads Liz's note that 'Wistia's analytics team mentors freshmen aggressively' → taps save.
     AI role: Editorial Note Writer drafts the advisor note from Liz's bullet-point inputs; Liz reviews and one-tap-approves in a SharePoint approval step.
     Outcome: Trust transfers: the Co-op office's authority gets injected into a surface Jordan already trusts.
  7. Year-in-Review: First-Year Co-op Wrapped
     Trigger: End of spring semester — Wrapped notification: 'Your first-year co-op taste, visualized.'
     Flow: Tap → full-screen Teams app pane animates through 6 slides: top mix, hearted roles, taste shift over time, peer overlap, advisor MVP, and a personalized 'so where do you go next?' card.
     AI role: Taste Profile Synthesizer narrates the journey from a 100% brand-name vector in September to a 60/40 SME-balanced vector in April; Gemini Imagen generates the slide hero imagery.
     Outcome: Jordan sees his own evolution — and shares the Wrapped card to his Snap story, organic peer-to-peer marketing of SME discovery.
  8. Collaborative Filter: 'Students Like You Hearted'
     Trigger: Jordan visits the Taste Profile tab.
     Flow: A 'Students like you' section shows 6 roles hearted by anonymized peers with overlapping taste vectors → each tile has the % overlap badge → Jordan taps to expand.
     AI role: Anonymized collaborative filter runs in Azure ML; FERPA-safe — only aggregate hearts, no individual student data exposed.
     Outcome: Jordan trusts peer signal more than algorithmic suggestion alone — applications follow.
  9. Tune Your Taste Profile
     Trigger: Jordan taps 'Refine' in the Taste Profile tab.
     Flow: Modal with 5 sliders: company size (startup ←→ enterprise), industry weight, location radius, mission focus, tech stack preference → Jordan adjusts → digest preview updates live.
     AI role: Recommender re-ranks the next digest in real time as sliders move; Gemini explains in plain English what just changed.
     Outcome: Jordan feels in control — the system isn't a black box, it's an instrument he plays.
  10. Director's Studio (Liz's view)
     Trigger: Liz logs into the Co-op Discovery SharePoint site Monday at 7 AM.
     Flow: Dashboard shows the 200 SME roles staged for this week's digests → Liz reviews the AI's quality scores → flags 3 to feature in Editorial → writes 2-sentence notes → one-tap approves the week.
     AI role: Quality scorer surfaces top SMEs by mentorship signal, alumni presence, and recency; Editorial Note Writer drafts Liz's blurbs from her shorthand.
     Outcome: Liz spends 18 minutes Monday morning shaping the experience for 3,400 first-years.

KEY SCREENS (10) — every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Discover Co-op Weekly (Teams Adaptive Card) — purpose: The Monday morning headline moment — 10 roles, 3 themed mixes, in a single scrollable card inside the Teams activity feed.
     Primary element: Album-art-style 2x5 grid of role tiles, each with company glyph, role title, mix-theme caption, and play button.
     Motion character: Tiles fade-in staggered 60ms apart on card open; hearted tiles pulse pink with a 240ms ease-out scale; skip tiles desaturate to grayscale over 180ms.
  2. Role Detail with Audio Brief — purpose: Deep-dive on a single role — audio narration, liner notes, the company's vibe in 30 seconds.
     Primary element: Hero image with embedded audio player, scrubber, 45s duration tag, and a Heart/Skip/Save action bar pinned to bottom.
     Motion character: Audio progress bar fills with a soft gradient sweep; on completion, the action bar bounces up 8px to invite a signal.
  3. Daily Mix Themed Carousel — purpose: Mid-week return surface — 4 Daily Mixes Jordan can browse like Spotify's home screen.
     Primary element: Horizontal scroll of large mix cards (Fintech Foundations, Boston Builders, Mission-Driven, Hidden Cambridge), each with generated cover art and a 3-role preview.
     Motion character: Parallax tilt on card hover (5° max); cover art generated by Imagen subtly animates with a Ken-Burns drift.
  4. Editorial Playlist (Liz's Picks) — purpose: Human-curated authority layer — feels like a New Yorker recommendation column inside Teams.
     Primary element: Vertical list of 5 roles, each with Liz's avatar, a 2-sentence handwritten-feeling note, and a 'save to your library' affordance.
     Motion character: Notes type in with a 28ms-per-character cadence the first time the card opens, then settle; Liz's avatar has a subtle breathing animation.
  5. Taste Profile — purpose: Jordan's portrait — the mirror that shows him what he's becoming.
     Primary element: Radar chart of 6 taste dimensions (industry, size, mission, location, stack, pace) with a current ring overlaid on a starting ring from September.
     Motion character: Radar morphs between weeks with a 600ms spring; the gap between September and Now ring gets a soft glow when the delta is large.
  6. Wrapped: First-Year Co-op Year — purpose: End-of-year emotional payoff and shareable artifact.
     Primary element: Full-bleed vertical-story-format slides, 6 of them, each a hero stat with generative imagery.
     Motion character: Slide transitions on tap with a 320ms cross-fade; each stat number counts up over 800ms with a cubic-bezier ease.
  7. Tune Your Taste (Refinement Modal) — purpose: Direct manipulation of the recommender — Jordan as the DJ.
     Primary element: Five horizontal sliders with live preview pane showing how next week's mix shifts as sliders move.
     Motion character: Preview tiles re-shuffle with FLIP animation (240ms ease-in-out) every time a slider settles for >300ms.
  8. Director's Studio (Liz's SharePoint View) — purpose: Backstage curation surface — where the Co-op office shapes what 3,400 students discover this week.
     Primary element: Three-column board: 'AI Surfaced' (200 roles), 'Editorial Featured' (5 slots), 'Live This Monday' (preview of student-facing digest).
     Motion character: Drag-and-drop with magnetic snap; approved cards slide to the right column with a 200ms ease and turn faintly green.
  9. NUworks Data Mapping View — purpose: Transparency layer (per user direction) — show exactly how a raw NUworks record becomes a Teams card.
     Primary element: Split-screen diagram: left shows raw NUworks JSON fields, right shows the rendered Teams adaptive card, animated connector lines mapping field-to-element.
     Motion character: Connector lines draw left-to-right with a 480ms stagger; on hover, the line and both endpoints highlight in NU red.
  10. Power Automate Flow Inspector — purpose: Engineering trust surface — Liz and Data Systems Admin see the flow in action.
     Primary element: Power Automate canvas chrome rendering 6 nodes: NUworks Export → Filter SME → Azure OpenAI Rewrite → TTS → SharePoint Cache → Teams Push, each with timestamp and run count.
     Motion character: Nodes pulse green as a simulated run flows through; the active edge glows for the duration of each step.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) — every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Themed Mix Composer (Headline Aha)
     User action: Opens Monday's Discover Co-op Weekly card.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Jordan's taste vector, declared major (Business Analytics), 200 NUworks SME roles passing the Director's quality filter, anonymized cohort heart history.
     Output: 10 roles bundled into exactly 3 themed mixes, each with a 5-7 word narrative label and a 1-sentence hook.
     User benefit: Discovery feels curated, not random — each mix reads like an editor wrote it for him.
  2. Audio Role Brief Generator
     User action: Taps the play icon on a role tile.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7 (script) + Azure Speech (TTS)
     Input: Raw NUworks JD, employer-submitted liner-note (60 words), Jordan's major.
     Output: 45-second second-person narrated MP3 cached in SharePoint, with a transcript fallback for accessibility.
     User benefit: Hands-free discovery during walks between classes; texture of a role comes through voice in ways text never delivers.
  3. Collaborative Filter on Anonymized Application History
     User action: Passive — runs nightly.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro embeddings + cosine similarity in Azure ML
     Input: Aggregate, k-anonymized (k≥10) heart and apply signals across the first-year cohort, joined to role embeddings.
     Output: Per-student ranked list of 50 candidate roles weekly, FERPA-compliant (no individual peer data exposed).
     User benefit: Peer wisdom amplifies advisor wisdom — 'students like you hearted' becomes a trust signal.
  4. Taste Profile Synthesizer
     User action: Views Taste Profile tab or end-of-year Wrapped.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Time-series of hearts, skips, applies, and slider adjustments; original September vector vs. current.
     Output: Plain-English narrative (90 words) describing how Jordan's taste has shifted, plus 6-dimension radar coordinates.
     User benefit: Jordan sees his own evolution articulated — a quiet, motivating mirror.
  5. Editorial Note Writer (Liz's Voice)
     User action: Liz types 3-bullet shorthand for a featured role in the Director's Studio.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Liz's bullets, the role's metadata, Liz's prior published notes (style sample).
     Output: Two polished sentences in Liz's voice — warm, specific, advisor-tone — surfaced for her one-tap approval.
     User benefit: Liz curates 5 roles in 18 minutes instead of 2 hours; her authority scales without burning her out.
  6. Skip-Reason Chip Classifier
     User action: Taps Skip and selects a reason chip ('too corporate', 'wrong city', 'unclear what I'd do').
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Skip chip + role metadata + Jordan's current taste vector.
     Output: Updated negative-space weights in the recommender; immediate confirmation toast: 'Got it — less of that next week.'
     User benefit: Negative signals are as valued as positive ones; the system gets out of his way fast.
  7. Wrapped Imagery Generator
     User action: Opens First-Year Co-op Wrapped in May.
     Model: Gemini Imagen
     Input: Taste profile delta, top-mix theme name, hearted-role geography.
     Output: 6 generative hero images per Wrapped slide — abstract, editorial, not photorealistic — matching NU's visual identity.
     User benefit: Wrapped feels like a personal artifact worth sharing, not a corporate dashboard.
  8. NUworks → Teams Field Mapper (Transparency)
     User action: Opens the NUworks Data Mapping View.
     Model: Wiki RAG over NUworks API documentation
     Input: A live NUworks role JSON record + the Teams adaptive card schema.
     Output: Annotated, animated map showing which JD field becomes which UI element, with FERPA-data-flow labels.
     User benefit: Liz, the Data Systems Admin, and skeptical faculty can see exactly how data flows — earns institutional trust.

SEED DATA — generate the FULL count of records per entity (not 1-3 example shapes — the actual full set):
  PRIMARY ENTITIES (2):
    • NUworks SME Role — target_count 28
      Shape: id, employer_name, employer_size, industry, role_title, location, hourly_rate, required_skills[], jd_raw, liner_note_employer, ai_rewritten_blurb, audio_brief_url, quality_score (0-100), mix_theme_tags[], hearts_count, posted_date, application_url, ferpa_flag
      Example records summary: Boston-area sub-200-employee company roles across analytics, fintech, healthtech, climate, marketing, and operations — each with a quality score, an employer liner-note, and a generated audio brief asset reference.
    • Student Taste Profile — target_count 25
      Shape: student_id (hashed), major, college, taste_vector_sept (6-dim), taste_vector_current (6-dim), hearts_total, skips_total, applies_total, top_mix_theme, last_active_at, wrapped_eligible, ferpa_consent_status
      Example records summary: Anonymized first-year profiles with declared major, evolving taste vector (Sept vs. current), hearts/skips/applies counts, and Wrapped-eligible flag.
  SECONDARY ENTITIES (5):
    • Themed Mix — target_count 12
      Shape: mix_id, theme_label, theme_hook_sentence, hero_image_url, member_role_ids[], generated_for_week, cohort_segment
      Example records summary: AI-composed weekly mixes with narrative labels, hero imagery, and 8-12 role members.
    • Editorial Pick (Liz's Picks) — target_count 15
      Shape: pick_id, role_id, advisor_name, advisor_note_2sentence, approved_at, week_of, featured_position
      Example records summary: Human-curated weekly picks with advisor note and approval timestamp.
    • Power Automate Flow Run — target_count 14
      Shape: run_id, started_at, completed_at, roles_processed, students_delivered, errors_count, avg_audio_gen_ms, status
      Example records summary: Telemetry from the weekly digest pipeline runs — useful for the Flow Inspector screen.
    • NUworks Raw JD Record — target_count 12
      Shape: nuworks_id, employer_org, position_title, description_html, qualifications, application_open, application_close, contact_email, restricted_to_ferpa
      Example records summary: Verbatim-style raw JSON pulled from NUworks for the Data Mapping screen.
    • Wrapped Slide — target_count 10
      Shape: slide_id, slide_type, headline, stat_value, narrative_caption, generated_image_url
      Example records summary: Slide definitions for the end-of-year Wrapped experience.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: playlist-card aesthetic, album-art tile grids, mixtape editorial energy, NU red accents on charcoal-and-cream Teams chrome, generative-but-restrained cover art, typography that whispers (Inter for UI, Tiempos for editorial notes), micro-motion over macro-motion
  Hero treatment: Each weekly digest opens with a hero strip showing three Daily Mix covers stacked at slight rotational offsets, like physical mixtapes. The covers are Imagen-generated — abstract gradient compositions with a single typographic mix-name overlaid. NU red appears only as accent (underlines, heart fills, mix-name punctuation). Background is a soft cream (#F7F4EE) in light mode, deep charcoal (#1A1A1C) in dark mode — Teams chrome respected. The entire experience feels like a thoughtfully designed magazine column dropped inside Teams, never a corporate dashboard.
  Motion character: Restrained and musical. Card unfurls use spring physics (stiffness 180, damping 16). Hearts pulse with a 240ms cubic-bezier and brief haptic. Mix covers have a Ken-Burns drift (3% scale over 8s, looping). FLIP animations on tile expansion at 320ms. Type uses typewriter cadence at 28ms/char for first-impression notes, then settles. Nothing slides faster than 480ms; nothing slower than 800ms. Audio waveforms pulse softly with the playing track.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these — the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. Imagen prompt: 'Abstract editorial cover art for a co-op mix titled Fresh Finds in Boston Analytics — soft gradient of teal and warm amber, faint geometric data-shapes layered like sediment, restrained, no text, magazine cover sensibility, 1:1 square.'
    2. Imagen prompt: 'Cover art for a mix titled Founders Under 40 — warm sunrise palette of cream and rust, abstract suggestion of a hand drawing a line, no faces, no text, painterly texture, 1:1 square.'
    3. Imagen prompt: 'Wrapped slide hero for a student whose taste shifted from brand-name to SME — split composition: left side dense crowd silhouette, right side single quiet workshop window with warm light, NU red accent line bridging them, no text overlay.'
    4. Imagen prompt: 'Cover art for a mix titled Hidden Cambridge — moody dusk gradient of slate and amber, abstract impression of brick and ivy, restrained, no people, no text, 1:1.'
    5. Imagen prompt: 'Cover art for Mission-Driven Mondays — soft sage and clay palette, abstract suggestion of a seedling and a circuit, hopeful but understated, no text, 1:1.'
    6. Imagen prompt: 'Editorial portrait-style abstract avatar for advisor Liz on Editorial Picks card — warm cream background, a single confident charcoal silhouette gesture, NU red accent collar, magazine columnist energy, no realistic face.'

FEATURE ROADMAP (4 phases) — the prototype demonstrates Phase 1 in working code; later phases appear as roadmap surfaces inside the experience:
  1. Phase 1 (Weeks 1-4) — The Monday Digest Foundation
     • Power Automate flow connecting NUworks daily batch export → SharePoint
     • Azure OpenAI rewrite pipeline for JD → conversational blurb (Claude Opus 4.7)
     • Teams adaptive-card digest delivery to opt-in pilot of 200 first-year analytics & business students
     • Heart / Skip / Save signal capture into SharePoint list
     • Director's Studio v1 in SharePoint for Liz's weekly approval ritual
     • FERPA data-flow documentation co-signed by Data Systems Admin
     Success: ≥60% of pilot students open at least one weekly digest in the first 4 weeks; ≥30% log at least one heart.
  2. Phase 2 (Months 2-3) — Discovery Intelligence
     • Themed Mix Composer goes live (Gemini 3.1 Pro) — 3 mixes per student weekly
     • Audio Role Brief generation (Claude script + Azure Speech TTS) cached in SharePoint
     • Collaborative filter on anonymized k≥10 cohort signals
     • 'Because You Hearted X' lookalike carousel in role detail
     • Skip-reason chip taxonomy and negative-signal learning loop
     • Editorial Picks workflow with one-tap advisor approval
     • Expand pilot to all 3,400 first-years across all colleges
     Success: +35% first-year applications to SME roles vs. prior cohort baseline; –15% applications to top-tier brand-name employers.
  3. Phase 3 (Months 4-9) — Taste & Wrapped
     • Taste Profile tab with 6-dimension radar and Sept-vs-Now overlay
     • Tune Your Taste refinement modal with live preview
     • First-Year Co-op Wrapped (May release) with Imagen-generated slide hero art and share-out artifact
     • Power BI dashboard for Co-op leadership tracking aperture-widening across the cohort
     • Faculty Coordinator alert flow for students whose taste vector stays brand-locked past November (proactive intervention)
     • Integration with CLR so hearted/applied-to SME activity contributes to the learner record
     Success: ≥45% of first-years voluntarily open Wrapped; ≥25% share it externally; CLR ingestion rate ≥95% of qualifying interactions.
  4. Phase 4 (Year 2) — Scale & Generalize
     • Extend Discover Co-op to sophomores and juniors with year-appropriate mix taxonomies
     • Employer-side Liner-Note Composer (Claude) so SME hiring managers contribute texture in 90 seconds
     • Cross-cohort 'Alumni Echoes' — past co-op alumni notes resurface on relevant SME roles
     • Multi-language audio briefs for international students
     • API exposure for sister institutions piloting the pattern
     Success: First-year SME placement share rises from baseline ~22% to ≥40%; Liz reports <20 minutes/week Director's Studio time.

NARRATIVE ARC (8 beats) — the multi-timeframe user journey the prototype must SUGGEST through copy, seed data, and roadmap surfaces:
  1. Minute 1 (Monday 8:03 AM, mid-September)
     User: Jordan's Teams pings during his walk to ISEC. He sees 'Discover Co-op Weekly is ready.' He taps it expecting another newsletter.
     AI: Themed Mix Composer has already run at 4 AM, scoring 213 SME roles against Jordan's freshly-minted taste vector and clustering the top 10 into three named mixes.
     Feeling: Curiosity, faintly suspicious — 'is this just an ad?'
  2. Minute 4 (same morning)
     User: Jordan taps play on Tessera Analytics. A 45-second second-person audio brief plays. He hearts it before he reaches Snell.
     AI: Claude's script + Azure TTS plays from SharePoint cache; heart signal logs instantly to the taste vector.
     Feeling: First small surprise — 'wait, that sounds kind of cool, and I've never heard of them.'
  3. Day 1
     User: Jordan revisits the digest twice during class breaks, hearts two more roles, skips one with reason 'too corporate.'
     AI: Skip-reason classifier nudges the negative-space weights; Tessera moves up in next week's slate; a similar Cambridge SaaS gets boosted.
     Feeling: Pleased — the system is listening, fast.
  4. Week 1
     User: Friday afternoon, Jordan sees Liz's Editorial Picks card. He reads her two-sentence note about Wistia and saves it.
     AI: Editorial Note Writer drafted Liz's note from her 3-bullet shorthand Monday morning; she approved in 11 seconds.
     Feeling: Trust transferring — 'if Liz vouches for them, I'll look.'
  5. Week 3
     User: Jordan opens his Taste Profile for the first time. The radar shows his Sept vector overlaid against his current — he's visibly drifted toward smaller, mission-driven, Cambridge-radius companies.
     AI: Taste Profile Synthesizer narrates the shift in 90 words: 'You started looking at companies over 10,000 people; you're now hearting teams of 40.'
     Feeling: Mild awe at his own evolution — and pride.
  6. Month 1
     User: Jordan submits applications to Tessera, Kettlewell, and Lumen — none of which were on his September radar. He also applies to Goldman, but it no longer feels like the only option.
     AI: Apply signals reweight the recommender; 'Students like you hearted' carousel begins showing Jordan to other freshmen as peer-signal.
     Feeling: Relief — there's a balanced portfolio under him for the first time.
  7. Month 3 (December)
     User: Jordan gets a first-round interview with Tessera. Walking in, he already knows the team vibe from the liner note. He nails it.
     AI: His application-to-interview conversion data anonymizes into the cohort filter, helping future students discover Tessera too.
     Feeling: Confidence — he prepared from texture, not from glassdoor scraping.
  8. Month 8 (May, end of freshman year)
     User: Wrapped notification arrives. Jordan swipes through six full-screen slides: top mix, taste shift, hearted count, peer overlap, advisor MVP (Liz), and where to go next. He screenshots slide 4 and texts it to his roommate.
     AI: Imagen generated six custom hero images overnight; Synthesizer drafted the captions in Jordan's voice patterns.
     Feeling: Pride and identity — 'I'm the kind of student who builds at SMEs.' Brand-fixation broken.

INTERACTION CHOREOGRAPHY (12 beats) — the step-by-step script for the HEADLINE aha interaction; honor the timing_ms values where given:
  1. Jordan unlocks his phone at 8:03 AM Monday during the walk to class and sees a Teams banner: 'Discover Co-op Weekly is ready — 10 fresh roles, just for you.'
     System: Teams notification badge increments; the Co-op Discovery bot rises to the top of Jordan's activity feed with an unread dot.
     Motion/feedback: Native Teams notification motion; subtle haptic on iOS.
  2. Jordan taps the notification.
     System: Teams opens to the Co-op Discovery chat; the adaptive card begins to unfurl.
     Motion/feedback: Card height animates from 0 to full with a soft spring; album-art tiles fade in staggered 60ms apart across the 2x5 grid. (480ms)
  3. Jordan scans the three mix labels at the top: 'Because you liked fintech', 'Fresh finds in Boston analytics', 'Founders under 40'.
     System: Mix labels render with a thin underline accent in NU red; a small AI sparkle glyph indicates each label is generated.
     Motion/feedback: Underline draws left-to-right over 200ms per label, staggered. (720ms)
  4. Jordan taps the Tessera Analytics tile — a sub-50-employee Cambridge analytics company he's never heard of.
     System: Tile expands inline into a role-detail card; audio player appears at the top with a 45s duration tag and Heart/Skip/Save action bar pinned at bottom.
     Motion/feedback: Tile expansion uses a FLIP morph (320ms ease-out); other tiles dim to 40% opacity. (320ms)
  5. Jordan taps the play button on the audio brief.
     System: MP3 streams from SharePoint cache; a second-person narration begins: 'Spend six months turning customer data into the stories that change Tessera's roadmap...'
     Motion/feedback: Progress bar fills with a soft NU-red gradient sweep; waveform glyph pulses gently in sync with audio. (200ms)
  6. Jordan listens for the full 45 seconds while walking, watching the waveform.
     System: Audio plays out; at the 40-second mark the action bar bounces up 8px to invite a signal.
     Motion/feedback: Bounce uses a spring(stiffness=180, damping=14); subtle haptic at the bounce moment. (45000ms)
  7. Jordan taps Heart.

=== CONSULTING BRIEF (every field below is mandatory grounding for the prototype) ===
Thesis: Actively combats brand-name hyper-fixation by scraping NUworks for high-quality SME roles and pushing them to first-year students via Teams.
Description (what gets built):
First-year undergraduate students arrive with rigid expectations, fixating on massive tech companies and ignoring the vast majority of available roles at small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs). This concept uses a Power Automate crawler to continuously scan the existing NUworks database for high-quality, non-brand-name opportunities. An Azure OpenAI layer evaluates the job descriptions against the student's declared major and early interests, rewriting the dry job descriptions into engaging, value-focused summaries. These hidden gems are then pushed directly to the student via a weekly Microsoft Teams digest. By proactively surfacing these roles in a surface the student already checks, the university broadens their aperture and prevents the massive disappointment of failing to secure a top-tier placement.
Why it matters for first-year undergraduate students:
First-year undergraduate students simply do not know what they do not know. As detailed in Theme 14, they lack the tools to discover high-quality SME opportunities. By bringing these roles directly to them, the tool reduces the anxiety of the search and prevents the self-sabotage of only applying to the top 1% of employers.
How it supports first-year undergraduate students outcomes over 18-24 months:
Broadening the search aperture early drastically improves the overall placement rate. When students apply to a balanced portfolio of employers, they secure interviews faster, experience less 'ghosting,' and ultimately match with roles that provide foundational skills, setting them up for greater success in subsequent co-op cycles.
Execution within Northeastern University's existing stack (named systems, connectors, AI layer location):
This solution leverages Power Automate to scrape or access via API the existing NUworks platform (which remains the system of record). Azure OpenAI processes the text, and Microsoft Teams acts as the delivery mechanism. It completely avoids the need to build a new 'job board' frontend, relying instead on automated, asynchronous communication through existing channels.
Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft 365, Teams, SharePoint, Power Automate, Power BI fit (named tools that reduce cost/burden):
This fits Jen's mandate perfectly by utilizing Power Automate as the integration tissue between the legacy system (NUworks) and the modern communication surface (Teams). It avoids the cost of procuring specialized third-party job discovery platforms by building a lightweight workflow using existing licenses.

  1. Strategic Co-op Director — Defining the criteria for a 'high-quality SME role'

  3. Liz — Approving the student communication strategy

state_machine.trigger: User taps on a role tile (e.g., Tessera Analytics)
side_effects: Fires 'audio_role_brief_generator' to fetch and cache audio script
Heart icon scales and turns NU red
Toast appears: 'Got it — more like Tessera in next Monday's mix.'
Fires 'lookalike_recommender' to render 'Because you hearted this' carousel
Fires 'skip_reason_classifier' upon chip selection to update negative space weights

state_machine.trigger: User taps Taste Profile tab in Teams
side_effects: Radar chart morphs from Sept to Current vector
Fires 'collaborative_filter_peers' to load 'Students like you' carousel

state_machine.trigger: Liz clicks 'View Data Mapping' on a staged role
side_effects: Fires 'nuworks_teams_mapper' to annotate the JSON-to-UI mapping

behavior_per_state.hover: Parallax tilt (5° max), cursor changes to pointer.
behavior_per_state.active: FLIP morph expansion (320ms ease-out) into detail view.
behavior_per_state.loading: Shimmer gradient sweeps left to right.

behavior_per_state.active: Scale 1.3, fill turns solid NU red, brief haptic feedback.
behavior_per_state.success: Scales back to 1.0, triggers success toast from bottom.

behavior_per_state.active: Fills with soft NU-red gradient sweep synced to audio time.

motion_contract.encodes: Focus and hierarchy — moving from browse mode to deep-dive mode without losing context.
Positive reinforcement — the system acknowledging the user's signal and confirming it was logged.
Evolution over time — visually proving to the student that their taste has shifted since September.
Human touch — making Liz's note feel handwritten and freshly authored rather than database-rendered.
Data lineage — proving transparency by showing exactly where each piece of information originated.

ai_flows.fires_on_trigger: Card load (simulating Monday 8 AM batch run)
ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a Spotify-style editorial curator for university co-ops. Group the provided SME roles into 3 themed mixes based on the student's major and taste vector. Write a 5-7 word narrative label and a 1-sentence hook for each.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Student Major: {{major}}. Taste Vector: {{taste_vector}}. Available Roles: {{roles_json}}. Generate 3 themed mixes.
ai_flows.renders_into: discover_weekly_teams_card hero strip and role groupings

ai_flows.fires_on_trigger: User taps play on a role tile
ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a conversational scriptwriter. Rewrite the dry NUworks job description and employer liner note into a compelling, second-person 45-second audio script that highlights the texture and impact of the role.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Raw JD: {{jd_raw}}. Liner Note: {{liner_note}}. Student Major: {{major}}. Write the script.
ai_flows.renders_into: role_detail_audio transcript fallback and TTS engine input

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a recommendation engine tuner. Analyze the user's skip reason for a specific role and output the updated negative-space weights for their taste vector.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Role: {{role_metadata}}. Skip Reason: {{skip_chip}}. Current Vector: {{taste_vector}}. Update the weights.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are an insightful career advisor. Compare the student's September taste vector to their current vector and write a 90-word plain-English narrative describing how their aperture has widened.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Sept Vector: {{vector_sept}}. Current Vector: {{vector_current}}. Recent Hearts: {{recent_hearts}}. Write the narrative.

ai_flows.fires_on_trigger: Liz types 3-bullet shorthand and clicks 'Draft Note'
ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are Liz, the Strategic Co-op Director. Expand 3 shorthand bullets into a warm, specific, 2-sentence advisor note recommending a role to first-year students.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Role: {{role_title}} at {{employer}}. Bullets: {{shorthand_bullets}}. Draft the note.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a data transparency engine. Map the fields from a raw NUworks JSON record to the corresponding UI elements in the Teams Adaptive Card schema, noting FERPA compliance rules.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Raw JSON: {{raw_json}}. Card Schema: {{card_schema}}. Generate the mapping.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a collaborative filtering engine. Given a hearted role, find 5 lookalike roles from the database and generate a short justification chip for each.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Hearted Role: {{role_id}}. Available Roles: {{roles_json}}. Find 5 lookalikes.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a k-anonymous peer recommendation engine. Find roles hearted by anonymized peers with overlapping taste vectors to the current user.
ai_flows.user_message_template: User Vector: {{taste_vector}}. Peer Cohort Data (k>=10): {{cohort_data}}. Return 6 roles.

brand_application.voice_tone: consulting-grade, restrained, declarative, no marketing copy, no hyperbole

critique.summary: The prototype achieves ~60% session coverage. While the core depth-first screens (Discover Weekly and Role Detail) are well-executed with functional AI integrations and motion, several critical interactive elements (Tune Taste modal, Apply buttons, Kanban drag-and-drop) are inert. Additionally, seed data density falls short of the requested targets and the AI fallback wrapper is missing OpenAI.

failed_sessions.missing_piece: Tune Taste button has no onClick handler; modal is missing.
Apply button on Role Detail is inert.
Kanban board lacks actual drag-and-drop state updates.
Apply via NUworks button on Data Mapping is inert.

issues.description: Multiple buttons lack onClick handlers (Tune Taste, Apply, Approve Week).
issues.fix: Wire buttons to state transitions, modals, or window.open calls.

issues.description: Seed data density is too low for Profiles, Mixes, and Raw JD.
issues.fix: Expand seed arrays to meet target counts (25, 12, 12 respectively).

issues.description: Kanban board in Director's Studio does not support actual drag-and-drop.
issues.fix: Implement HTML5 drag-and-drop event handlers to update column state.

issues.description: AI fallback helper is missing OpenAI as the final fallback provider.
issues.fix: Add OpenAI to the providers array in callAIWithFallback.
